question: An engineer must affirm the identity of the Cisco UCS Manager after a valid CA-signed keyring for HTTPS access is created. Which action completes the configuration?
theory: After a CA-signed keyring is created for HTTPS, Cisco UCS Manager still needs a way to validate that certificate's chain of trust; creating a trusted point (which holds the issuing CA's certificate) lets UCS Manager confirm the keyring's certificate is authoritative before binding it to the HTTPS service. This mirrors the same PKI trust-chain concept used elsewhere (e.g., trusting a remote LDAP server's root CA certificate) to affirm a device's identity for secure communications. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 19 - Securing UCS Management, PKI/trusted points)
